prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universally “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact location, budget, equipment preference, home size, and how important things like speed, warranties, and energy-efficiency are. I can help you find the best option for your situation. A few quick questions will let me give specific recommendations:

- What Atlanta zip code or neighborhood are you in?
- Approximate home size and number of zones/rooms served by the system?
- Do you have brand or efficiency (SEER) preferences?
- When do you need the replacement done (ASAP vs. a few weeks)?
- Rough budget or financing needs?

While you answer, here are practical steps and criteria to pick a top-quality HVAC contractor in Atlanta:

What to look for
- Proper licensing and insurance: verify Georgia contractor license (and general liability) before hiring.
- NATE-certified technicians and company affiliations (ACCA, local trade groups) indicate training and professionalism.
- Experience with your type/size of system and with load calculations (ask for a Manual J heat-load calculation).
- Clear written estimate (equipment, labor, permits, removal of old unit, refrigerant handling, and total cost).
- Good local reviews (Google, Yelp, Angi) and A+ or good standing with the BBB.
- Strong labor and manufacturer warranties (get terms in writing).
- Proper permitting and code-compliant installation (make sure they pull permits).
- Energy-efficiency options and knowledge of rebates/incentives (Georgia Power and others sometimes offer rebates).

Questions to ask each contractor
- Are your technicians NATE-certified? Can you show proof of license/insurance?
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation? Will the quote reflect that?
- Exactly what brand/model and SEER rating are you recommending? Why?
- What’s included in the price (thermostat, condensate handling, permits, duct modifications)?
- What are the warranty terms (parts and labor)? Is there a callback policy?
- How long will the installation take and when can you start?
- Can you provide recent local references?

Price expectations (ballpark)
- Full central AC replacement in Atlanta typically ranges roughly $3,500–$10,000+ depending on unit size (tons), SEER rating, ductwork modifications, and complexity. Get at least three written quotes to compare.

Where to find reputable contractors
- Search Google/Yelp for “HVAC replacement Atlanta” and sort by reviews.
- Check Angi (Angie’s List) and the Better Business Bureau.
- Ask neighbors/homeowners groups for referrals.
- Get referrals from local utility (rebate program partners).

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-rated HVAC contractors in your specific Atlanta zip code and provide a short list (with review summaries).
- Help compare 2–3 written quotes if you paste them here.
Tell me your zip code and any preferences and I’ll pull targeted recommendations.
